key_insight: Active learning makes interatomic potential development more data-efficient by iteratively targeting the most informative configurations, but its success depends on trustworthy uncertainty estimates.
engineering_relevance: This review is directly relevant for building reliable ML interatomic potentials that generalize to the real operating conditions of materials and chemistry simulations, reducing expensive reference calculations.
method: Close the loop: generate candidates, estimate uncertainty, select data, compute reference labels, and update the model.
Use uncertainty-driven acquisition with on-the-fly MD, committee methods, Gaussian processes, or frozen pretrained models.
Apply AL across diverse systems, including alloys, diffusion, ferroelectrics, reactive chemistry, and disordered materials.
evidence_signal: The review synthesizes more than seventy studies, with emphasis on work from 2020 to 2026, spanning multiple application areas and active-learning strategies.
watch_item: Uncertainty estimates are not interchangeable across model architectures and can be least reliable exactly in the regimes where the model most needs guidance.
paper_title: Active Learning for Interatomic Potentials: A Review of Uncertainty-Driven Data Efficiency
